clue.text: The youngster embracing her is an innocent child

indicators.note: the young animal's word holds the next piece in its arms, so it goes around it

parts.note: a cub is a young animal, or a young scout
taken as written

explanation.surface: A remark that a child hugging a woman is a picture of innocence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The youngster' looks like the definition, but the child is defined at the end; 'embracing' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A cherub is a winged angel-child of art, so the word is used for any sweet, guileless little one.

clue.text: New deal receiving attention? It's a bluff

indicators.note: the word for attention takes in the rearranged letters, so it goes around them

parts.note: hand in the sense of care given, as in being in good hands

indicators.note: a new version of a word has its letters arranged differently

explanation.surface: Asks whether a fresh agreement is being noticed, then calls it a bluff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges the four letters of 'deal'; 'receiving' is the container signal. 'bluff' is the noun for a cliff, not a deception.
explanation.definitionFit: A bluff is a steep cliff or promontory, and a headland juts out to sea in the same way.

clue.text: Bands I'd hear from this seat

indicators.note: the words are to be taken as they sound when spoken

parts.note: rings are bands, and I'd is spoken as the letter-word 'eyed'

explanation.surface: A spectator saying which seat gives the best view of the bands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hear' says RINGS I'D, spoken, gives the seat next to a boxing ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringside seat is one right beside the boxing or circus ring.

clue.text: FE Smith, for one — good man in obstruction case

indicators.note: the holy man's abbreviation is placed within the word for a blockage

parts.note: a barrier is an obstruction; it acts as a case around the next piece
ST, for saint, is a good man

explanation.surface: A famous lawyer described as a good man caught up in a blocked legal case.
explanation.walkthrough: F E Smith, Lord Birkenhead, was a celebrated English lawyer and Lord Chancellor. 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: F E Smith was a famous advocate at the English bar before becoming Lord Chancellor.

clue.text: Hercules, perhaps, advancing with difficulty?

parts.note: Hercules performed twelve famous labours, so he is one who toils; and someone moving forward with difficulty is said to be toiling along in that sense too

explanation.surface: The mythical strongman struggling forward on one of his tasks.
explanation.walkthrough: The Twelve Labours of Hercules give the first reading; 'labouring' also means making slow, hard progress, which gives the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A manual worker who toils is a natural description of Hercules at his twelve tasks.

clue.text: Royal attendants dig. Italian wines, it turns out

indicators.note: what turns out is produced in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Courtiers are told to plant Italian wines, which then turn out badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it turns out' rearranges the fifteen letters of DIG ITALIAN WINES.
explanation.definitionFit: Ladies-in-waiting are women of rank who attend a queen or princess at court.

clue.text: Receiver's illegal act.

parts.note: the possessive 's is read as 'of', and a receiver of stolen goods is a fence
the possessive 's is read as 'of', and a receiver of stolen goods is a fence

explanation.surface: Handling stolen goods described as a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Receiver's' as 'of receiver', with a fence being a dealer in stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: An offence is a breach of the law, a crime.

clue.text: Instrument to study, say, on the Tube

indicators.note: the word for studying is taken as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it at university
a pipe is a tube

explanation.surface: A suggestion to study a musical instrument while riding the London Underground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Tube' is London's Underground in the surface but just a tube here. 'say' turns READ into REED.
explanation.definitionFit: A reed pipe is a simple wind instrument, or an organ pipe sounded by a reed.

clue.text: Confine, heartless trickster for imposture

indicators.note: an imposture is a deception, a disguise, so the letters are presented in a false arrangement
the middle letter of the swindler's word is removed

explanation.surface: A cheat without a heart is to be locked up for his fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes K, the middle of TRICKSTER, leaving TRICSTER; 'for imposture' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: To restrict is to keep something within limits, to hem it in.

clue.text: Having a crew including engineers displaying affectation

indicators.note: the crewed word takes the next piece inside itself, so it surrounds it

parts.note: a ship with a crew is manned
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: A boat with engineers among its crew is behaving in a showy, put-on way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'including' is the container signal; RE (Royal Engineers) is a common crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Mannered behaviour is artificial and stilted, full of put-on airs.

clue.text: Bids made by colonels, possibly, when not in charge

indicators.note: says the following abbreviation must be absent from the word for military ranks

parts.note: colonels are an example of army officers

explanation.surface: Senior army men putting in bids once they are no longer in command.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when not' removes IC from OFFICERS. 'possibly' marks colonels as just one kind of officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A bid is a proposal of a price, and offers are exactly such proposals.

clue.text: Berry Alice swallowed initially, lacking sweets perhaps

indicators.note: the girl's name takes the following letters into herself, so they go inside her

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: points to the opening letter of each of the three words that follow

explanation.surface: A girl gulps down a berry because she has no sweets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes the first letters of 'lacking sweets perhaps'; 'swallowed' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Allspice is the dried fruit of a West Indian tree, a berry used whole or ground as a spice.

clue.text: One picking off birds by river

parts.note: snipe are long-billed wading birds; the plural is the same as the singular
R is a standard abbreviation for river on maps

explanation.surface: A hunter shooting birds beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: Snipe-shooting is where the word for a marksman picking targets off came from, so the surface is apt.
explanation.definitionFit: A marksman who shoots individual targets from cover picks them off one by one.

clue.text: Need a tie designed for a political prisoner

indicators.note: something designed is put together in a new form, so the letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A man held for his politics asks for a tie to be made for him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' rearranges the eight letters of NEED A TIE.
explanation.definitionFit: A person held in custody without trial, often for political reasons, is one detained by the state.

clue.text: Call-up turned into a discharge

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for a call is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to call someone something is to name them

indicators.note: turned means the following short words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A conscription notice that became a dismissal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses NAME to EMAN; 'turned' rearranges INTO A to ATION.
explanation.definitionFit: An emanation is something that flows out or is given off, such as a gas or radiation.

clue.text: The advantage of keenness.

definitions.meaning: to have the upper hand over a rival

explanation.surface: A remark that eagerness gives you a head start.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a slight lead over others, as in having it over a rival; the other is a blade's sharpness.

clue.text: Huge rodent with tail raised and not caught in it

indicators.note: the joining word is trapped inside the altered animal word
in a down clue, the final letter of the animal's name goes up to the top

parts.note: a mouse is a small rodent
nor means and not

explanation.surface: A giant rat holding its tail high, not caught in a trap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with tail raised' moves the rodent's last letter to the top, giving EMOUS; 'caught in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Enormous means vast, immensely large.

clue.text: Exercises a Chinese emperor first put together for an equestrian event

indicators.note: the ruler's title is placed before the single letter, not after it as the clue order suggests

parts.note: gym is physical training, exercises
a khan was a Mongol ruler of China, such as Kublai

explanation.surface: Training plus an emperor's contribution, combined to make a horse show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' puts KHAN ahead of A. Kublai Khan, the Mongol, was emperor of China.
explanation.definitionFit: A gymkhana is a meeting with horse-riding contests, especially for children on ponies.

clue.text: Six-footer not at home in this dissenting group

indicators.note: says the word for being at home is to be taken away from the creature's name

parts.note: an insect has six legs, so it is a six-footer
in means at home, as in 'staying in'

explanation.surface: Someone who is out when a member of a breakaway faction calls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Six-footer' looks like a tall person but means a six-legged creature; 'not' removes IN from INSECT.
explanation.definitionFit: A sect is a small breakaway body that has split from a larger religious group.

clue.text: Drawings illustrating various points about a boat

indicators.note: the compass letters go around the vessel's name

parts.note: S, E and S are compass points
a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat

explanation.surface: Pictures showing several features of a yacht.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal; 'various points' are compass letters, a common crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Sketches are rough drawings made quickly.

clue.text: Officer-and other rank meet trouble in this desert

parts.note: COL is the abbreviation for colonel, an officer
OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers
ado means fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: An officer and a private run into difficulty in a desert.
explanation.walkthrough: The Colorado Desert lies in southern California.
explanation.definitionFit: The Colorado Desert is an arid region of south-east California, part of the Sonoran.

clue.text: The disadvantage of a hospital room?

definitions.meaning: a hospital room is a ward; that word written back to front, as the question mark hints, is the first half of the answer

explanation.surface: A complaint about what is wrong with a hospital ward.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is a playful split: the first four letters, taken back, spell a hospital room.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a snag that counts against something; the other jokes that a ward, read back, spells the first part.

clue.text: Decline some French currency

parts.note: des is French for 'some' with plural nouns
a cent is a coin, a unit of currency

explanation.surface: The fall in value of part of the French money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some French' wants a French currency; it gives DES.
explanation.definitionFit: A descent is a downward slope or a fall, a decline.

clue.text: Like a Hogarth subject seemingly built for speed

definitions.meaning: Hogarth's series The Rake's Progress follows a dissolute young man
a ship with a streamlined, sloping look seems made to go fast

explanation.surface: A painter's dashing figure who looks made to move fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seemingly' links the definitions: a raked mast or hull looks swift.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense describes a dissolute pleasure-seeker like Hogarth's Tom Rakewell; the other a vessel with a smart, streamlined look.

clue.text: A lull during the fighting, say?

definitions.meaning: soldiers engaged in battle are said to be busy in combat; the question mark admits the phrase is split

explanation.surface: A pause in the middle of a battle.
explanation.walkthrough: Split it as IN ACTION for the second reading: the opposite of the first.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is idleness or a halt in activity; the other, split in two, means engaged in combat.

clue.text: Iron Age ruse for concealing a stone-thrower

indicators.note: the three words keep the answer's letters tucked away across their boundaries

explanation.surface: A trick from prehistory used to keep a siege weapon out of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concealing' points to the letters running across irON AGE Ruse.
explanation.definitionFit: An onager was a Roman siege catapult that hurled stones, named after the kicking wild ass.

clue.text: Down town, possibly, his birthplace

parts.note: Down is a county of Northern Ireland, so a man born in a town in County Down is from Ireland

explanation.surface: Someone born in the city centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down town' reads as the city centre, but Down is a county in Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A man born in an Irish county such as Down is a native of Ireland.

clue.text: Jumping like a sailor in pain.

indicators.note: the seaman's word is placed within the word for a sharp pain

parts.note: a sting is a sharp, smarting pain
tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman leaping about because he is hurting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'like a' is a link; 'in' is the container signal, and tar is an old word for a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: To start is to jump suddenly with surprise or fright.

clue.text: For an old man; an alternative retreat comes first

indicators.note: the word for a retreat is placed before the word for an alternative

parts.note: a nest is a snug hideaway or refuge
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: Advice to an elderly man: put your home before other options.
explanation.walkthrough: Nestor, the aged and wise king of Pylos in Homer, gives his name to any wise old man.
explanation.definitionFit: In Homer, the elderly counsellor of the Greeks at Troy, so his name stands for any venerable elder.
